claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces resonant phonon-scattering centers.
SRO increases the anharmonicity of the local potential-energy landscape.
MoNbTaW is a bcc refractory high-entropy alloy.
High-temperature homogenization followed by water quenching produces a chemically disordered RHEA state with negligible SRO.
Thermomechanical aging or controlled cooling can induce SRO without causing long-range phase separation.
L12- or L11-type motifs are representative SRO motifs that can be induced in the proposed bcc RHEA.
Phonons are the dominant heat carriers in the alloy between 300 K and 1000 K.
SRO produces local lattice distortions that act as mass-fluctuation and strain-field scattering centers for phonons.
SRO produces alternating Cr-Co/Ni chemical planes.
In NiCoCr, Cr preferentially bonds with Ni and Co.
Preferential chemical bonding creates local regions with distinct vibrational densities of states that resonantly scatter mid- to high-frequency phonons.
The proposed SRO-induced scattering increases the phonon scattering rate, decreases phonon mean free path, and thereby lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Evidence that SRO impedes dislocation motion supports an analogous impediment to phonon propagation.
An aged, high-SRO sample will have more than 10% lower total thermal conductivity than a water-quenched control.
The predicted thermal-conductivity decrease will be driven primarily by a reduction in the lattice component.
The electronic thermal-conductivity component may increase slightly or remain stable because ordering reduces electron scattering.
In the disordered baseline, phonon scattering is dominated by random mass and strain fluctuations.
The proposed effect may fail when SRO produces coherent long-range-ordered precipitates or is too weak to alter the vibrational density of states.
A confirmed SRO-parameter increase greater than 0.1 accompanied by either an increase in lattice thermal conductivity or a change smaller than 2% is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
